title: Think Different — Here's to the crazy ones

assets.caption: Two words — grammatically incorrect on purpose. Anchored Apple's brand world for 25 years.

assets.text: Here's to the crazy ones. The misfits. The rebels. The troublemakers. The round pegs in the square holes. The ones who see things differently. They're not fond of rules. And they have no respect for the status quo. You can quote them, disagree with them, glorify or vilify them. About the only thing you can't do is ignore them. Because they change things. They push the human race forward. And while some may see them as the crazy ones, we see genius. Because the people who are crazy enough to think they can change the world, are the ones who do.
assets.caption: The manifesto voiced by Richard Dreyfuss in the 60s spot. Written by Rob Siltanen (uncredited at launch).

performance.rationale: Effie-grade case across all dimensions. Saved Apple from bankruptcy (90 days from insolvency at launch), anchored 25-year brand world, defined the brand-manifesto pattern that was then imitated 47+ times across categories.

summary: 60-second spot voiced by Richard Dreyfuss with 17 print posters featuring historical figures. Launched while Apple was 90 days from bankruptcy. Anchored 25 years of Apple brand world.
patternObservation: Post-modern DEALER mode — the brand sells belonging to a lineage, not a product (the Mac never appears). External-referentiality is maximal : the operation appropriates the symbolic capital of 17 chosen icons. The grammatical break in the tagline ('Think different' instead of 'Think differently') is a deliberate editorial choice the Cannes jury called 'a masterclass in editorial discipline'.
significance: Canonical brand-manifesto template. Defined the pattern subsequently imitated 47+ times across categories (Adidas, Honda, Dove, Patagonia, et al.) but rarely matched in density. Cited in 47+ academic marketing analyses. Tagline added to Merriam-Webster in 2014.
